title: SYNDACTYLY, TYPE III
alt_titles: SYNDACTYLY OF FINGERS IV AND V

intro.text: This entry describes syndactyly type III (SDTY3), also called syndactyly of the ring and little fingers. In the supplied reports it was mapped to chromosome 6q22-q24.

checks.claim: Syndactyly type III (SDTY3) is also called syndactyly of the ring and little fingers.
checks.evidence_quote: familial syndactyly of the ring and little finger (Type III syndactyly)
checks.explanation: The abstract treats type III syndactyly and syndactyly of the ring and little finger as the same condition.

checks.claim: Syndactyly type III (SDTY3) was mapped to chromosome 6q22-q24.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly, but atypical facial features, further suggested that isolated type III syndactyly is also located in this same region of the genome.
checks.explanation: The 6q22-q24 assignment (title) is for the ODD locus. The paper only suggests that isolated type III syndactyly maps to the same region, based on one family. It does not report a firm mapping of SDTY3 to 6q22-q24.

paragraphs.text: Type III syndactyly is fusion between the ring and little fingers (fingers 4 and 5). It occurs as an isolated, autosomal dominant hand malformation, and expression is variable (McKiernan and McCann, 1993; De Smet et al., 1994). Type III syndactyly is also a feature of oculodentodigital dysplasia (ODD), and several authors have asked whether the 2 conditions form a single clinical spectrum (Brueton et al., 1990; Schrander-Stumpel et al., 1993; Gladwin et al., 1997).

checks.claim: Type III syndactyly is fusion between the ring and little fingers (fingers 4 and 5).
checks.evidence_quote: familial syndactyly of the ring and little finger (Type III syndactyly)
checks.explanation: Ring and little fingers are fingers 4 and 5.

checks.claim: Type III syndactyly occurs as an isolated, autosomal dominant hand malformation.
checks.evidence_quote: Five new cases of isolated syndactyly of the small and ring finger are described. Autosomal dominant inheritance is obvious.
checks.explanation: Isolated occurrence and autosomal dominant inheritance are both stated.

checks.claim: Expression of type III syndactyly is variable.
checks.evidence_quote: clinical study reveals variable phenotypical expression
checks.explanation: The abstract states that expression is variable.

checks.claim: Type III syndactyly is a feature of oculodentodigital dysplasia (ODD).
checks.evidence_quote: A family is described with type III syndactyly and facies resembling the oculodentodigital dysplasia facial phenotype in the absence of any of the other characteristic findings of the latter condition.
checks.explanation: The phrase 'other characteristic findings' of ODD means type III syndactyly is treated as one of ODD's characteristic findings.

checks.claim: Several authors have asked whether type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia form a single clinical spectrum.
checks.evidence_quote: Oculodentodigital dysplasia and type III syndactyly: separate genetic entities or disease spectrum?
checks.explanation: This paper is one of the authors who ask whether the two conditions form a single spectrum. The word 'several' depends on the other papers cited.

paragraphs.text: Opjordsmoen and Nyberg-Hansen (1980) reported a family from northern Norway in which 9 of 22 members across 3 generations had spastic paraplegia, neurogenic bladder disturbances, and syndactyly. The bladder disturbance was an incomplete supranuclear bladder paresis (uninhibited neurogenic bladder). It was the main complaint and appeared early in the disease. The authors thought the family probably represented an unusual form of hereditary spastic paraplegia.

checks.explanation: Syndactylia is the same as syndactyly.

paragraphs.text: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) reported a newborn boy with complete cutaneous syndactyly of fingers 3 to 5 on the left hand and fingers 4 and 5 on the right hand. His mother and maternal grandmother were born with the same hand malformation. The mother had a thin nose and small teeth. The grandmother had very small teeth with enamel hypoplasia. Both women had normal eyes. The authors considered the family evidence of variable expression in oculodentodigital dysplasia.

paragraphs.text: McKiernan and McCann (1993) reported a pedigree with 14 cases of familial syndactyly of the ring and little fingers. Expression of the phenotype varied. Four of the affected individuals had been treated surgically.

checks.evidence_quote: We present a pedigree containing 14 cases of familial syndactyly of the ring and little finger (Type III syndactyly).
checks.explanation: The abstract gives the 14 cases directly.

checks.claim: Expression of the ring and little finger syndactyly phenotype varied in the pedigree reported by McKiernan and McCann (1993).
checks.evidence_quote: clinical study reveals variable phenotypical expression
checks.explanation: The abstract states that expression varied.

checks.claim: Four of the affected individuals in the pedigree reported by McKiernan and McCann (1993) had been treated surgically.
checks.evidence_quote: Three of these were treated surgically in this unit, and a fourth had previously been treated elsewhere by the senior author of this paper.
checks.explanation: Three were treated in the authors' unit and one elsewhere, making four treated surgically.

paragraphs.text: De Smet et al. (1994) described 5 new cases of isolated syndactyly of the ring and small fingers. Brachymesophalangy of the fifth finger was a frequent association.

checks.claim: De Smet et al. (1994) described 5 new cases of isolated syndactyly of the ring and small fingers.
checks.evidence_quote: Five new cases of isolated syndactyly of the small and ring finger are described.
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

checks.claim: Brachymesophalangy of the fifth finger was a frequent association in the cases of isolated ring and small finger syndactyly described by De Smet et al. (1994).
checks.evidence_quote: Brachymesophalangia of the fifth finger is a frequent association.
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

paragraphs.text: Analysis of a large pedigree by McKiernan and McCann (1993) confirmed autosomal dominant inheritance of type III syndactyly. De Smet et al. (1994) also observed autosomal dominant inheritance. Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) found autosomal dominant inheritance in a 3-generation family with type III syndactyly and features of ODD.

checks.claim: Analysis of a large pedigree by McKiernan and McCann (1993) confirmed autosomal dominant inheritance of type III syndactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of the pedigree confirms the autosomal dominant nature of the genetic defect
checks.explanation: The abstract also calls this one of the largest pedigrees reported, which supports 'large pedigree'.

checks.claim: De Smet et al. (1994) observed autosomal dominant inheritance of type III syndactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: Autosomal dominant inheritance is obvious.
checks.explanation: Autosomal dominant inheritance of ring and small finger syndactyly is stated.

checks.claim: Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) found autosomal dominant inheritance in a 3-generation family with type III syndactyly and features of oculodentodigital dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: The mother and maternal grandmother were born with the same hand malformation. Facial features in the mother showed a thin nose and small teeth; eyes were normal. In the grandmother, teeth had been very small with enamel hypoplasia; eyes were normal.
checks.explanation: Grandmother, mother and son make 3 generations with type III syndactyly and ODD features, and the abstract states: 'Inheritance is autosomal dominant.'

paragraphs.text: Gladwin et al. (1997) carried out a genome search and mapped the oculodentodigital syndrome locus to chromosome 6q22-q24 (maximum pairwise lod score of 9.37 at theta = 0.001). Their analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly and atypical facial features suggested that isolated type III syndactyly maps to the same region.

checks.claim: Gladwin et al. (1997) carried out a genome search and mapped the oculodentodigital syndrome locus to chromosome 6q22-q24.
checks.evidence_quote: a total genome search for the location of the ODD locus was instigated and linkage to polymorphic markers located on chromosome 6q established
checks.explanation: The title gives the 6q22-q24 localization.

checks.claim: Gladwin et al. (1997) obtained a maximum pairwise lod score of 9.37 at theta = 0.001 for the oculodentodigital syndrome locus on chromosome 6q22-q24.
checks.evidence_quote: linkage to polymorphic markers located on chromosome 6q established (pairwise Zmax = 9.37; theta = 0.001)
checks.explanation: The lod score and theta value match the paper.

checks.claim: Gladwin et al. (1997) analyzed a large family with type III syndactyly and atypical facial features.
checks.evidence_quote: Analysis of a large family with type III syndactyly, but atypical facial features
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Analysis by Gladwin et al. (1997) suggested that isolated type III syndactyly maps to the same chromosome 6q22-q24 region as oculodentodigital syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: further suggested that isolated type III syndactyly is also located in this same region of the genome.
checks.explanation: The draft's word 'suggested' matches the paper's own hedging.

paragraphs.text: Brueton et al. (1990) and Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) discussed whether type III syndactyly and oculodentodigital dysplasia are separate genetic entities or parts of one clinical spectrum. Schrander-Stumpel et al. (1993) interpreted their family as showing variable expression of ODD. Paznekas et al. (2003) found mutations in the GJA1 (connexin-43) gene in all 17 families with ODD they screened, and noted that type III syndactyly occurs in some cases of ODD. Richardson et al. (2004) reported that expression of Gja1 correlated with the phenotype seen in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.

checks.evidence_quote: Oculodentodigital dysplasia and type III syndactyly: separate genetic entities or disease spectrum?
checks.explanation: Both the title and the abstract's statement that the relationship is discussed support this.

checks.explanation: The title frames the conditions as one spectrum, but the abstract does not show the authors explicitly discussing whether they are separate genetic entities.

checks.evidence_quote: The present family provides evidence of the variable expression in oculodentodigital dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Paznekas et al. (2003) found mutations in the GJA1 (connexin-43) gene in all 17 families with oculodentodigital dysplasia they screened.
checks.evidence_quote: We found mutations in the GJA1 gene in all 17 families with oculodentodigital dysplasia that we screened.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.explanation: The abstract says type III syndactyly can occur in some cases of ODD.

checks.claim: Richardson et al. (2004) reported that expression of Gja1 correlated with the phenotype seen in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.
checks.evidence_quote: Expression of Gja1 correlates with the phenotype observed in oculodentodigital syndrome/type III syndactyly.
checks.explanation: The claim restates the paper's title directly. Only the title was supplied.
